EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: JUMP BASICS Sat 8-11 & JUMP PROGRESSION Sun 8-11
EventNotes:
The Ride Series is different. Your expectations should be high as you enter the hospitality of our classroom setting. A comfortable Kijaro chair awaits your presence and the cover our 10x20 tents provides reprieve from the elements. Prepare yourself to be immersed in an environment that provides the perfect opportunity for you to be open to embracing and practicing the proper technique. Instant feedback from our coaching staff will have you progressing like never before! Are YOU ready??

JUMP ESSENTIALS: 

We get it, everyone wants to jump! However, most people don't embrace the technique AND psychology behind doing it well. You have to understand the what and why before you can start to build confidence with the how, that's what this session is for. Not only will you build a solid understanding of what NEEDS to happen, you'll also get plenty of reps working through the steps of how it needs to happen, all in a safe and controlled environment. 

Topics Covered: 

Riders will get plenty of reps on multiple takeoffs/landings and Rich will work through multiple rounds of video so you can see exactly what's working and what isn't. 

JUMP PROGRESSION Session: Ground School and All American Hero's Jumpline

This event is all about getting comfortable in the air. That starts with a solid understanding of what it takes to get into the air properly. It's also critical to get as MANY reps as possible in a controlled environment and that's what the TRS ground school setting gives you.

Rich will break down the dynamics involved with jumping a bike. Based on over 40 years of experience, he will guide you through his real world experience and provide key insight and cues on what to do. 

After showcasing the proper technique, you'll work through a series of reps and the distance will incrementally increase as your comfort level increases. Analysis and feedback using slow motion video will have you "busting big" in no time.

There's no substitute for experience when it comes to jumping a bike. The only problem is that experience in the right setting can be hard to come by. You'll get tons reps on our jump lines and receive valuable feedback in the moment.
RIDERS MUST HAVE:
- Experience jumping
- Full suspension bikes with suspension in working order
- Full safety gear including pads (Full Face helmet not required, but suggested)

This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

Please reach out if you are unsure if this class is a proper fit for you.

Cranky Monkey Mountain Bike Race

The Cranky Monkey heads to Rosaryville State Park in 2026!  Join us for an awesome day of bike racing and community.

Race Date: Sunday August 30, 2026 (rain date 9/27)

Race Courses: 4 XC courses varying in length from about 6 miles miles to over 30 miles.  See course notes below for course information and maps.

  • Beginner – 5.6ish miles
  • Base –  9ish miles
  • Sport – 20ish miles
  • Expert – 30ish miles

Rosaryville State Park in Upper Marlboro, MD is an absolute gem and one of the most beginner friendly and fun parks in our area for mountain biking. We’ve been hosting races at Rosaryville for over 15 years and are excited to bring back the Cranky Monkey to this very special park. We’ve designed four courses for this race – beginner, base, sport, and expert. They are each described below. All courses start and end at the day use pavilions near the power lines that traverse the park. The start of the race is designed to allow for an exciting, but not overly crowded race start.

  • Beginner (~5.6 miles) – the beginner course is just shy of 6 miles long with about 400 feet of elevation change. It is designed to provide a safe and achievable entrance to mountain bike racing for participants of a variety of ages. The course highlights the western portion of the Perimeter Trail, which is the main multi-use trail in the park.
  • Base (~9 miles) – the base course is a step up fro the beginner course both in length and difficulty. It is about 9 miles in length with 600 feet of elevation change. The base course also highlights the western portion of the Perimeter Trail and also adds in the more technical Tilly Trail.
  • Sport (~20 miles) – the sport course provides a grand tour of the Rosaryville trail system and comes in at about 20 miles in length with about 1,500 feet of elevation change. The sport course highlights the entire Perimeter and Tilly Trails plus a bit.
  • Expert (~30 miles) – the expert course provides a grand route of the Rosaryville trail system and comes in about about 30 miles in length with about 2,200 feet of elevation change. The expert course highlights two complete loops of the Perimeter and Tilly Trails plus a bit.

All the trails at Rosaryville are largely maintained by volunteers organized by the Mid-Atlantic Off-Road Enthusiasts (MORE).  All racers will have the opportunity to donate to the Rosaryville Trail Fund during registration.

Race Day Schedule
Sunday August 30, 2026 (rain date 9/27)

  • 8:00am – Beginner race start
  • 9:00am – Base race start
  • 10:00am – Sport and Expert races start

Race Start Procedures
We are separating each race into wave starts to allow enough space to spread out the field of riders.  Each wave will be separated by a few minutes. Exact start times will be based on the number of riders in each class.

EventName: Bike Hub Sunday Epic V5 - Grass Mtn Sufferfest
EventNotes:
The Bike Hub is proud to announce our Sunday Epic ride series! These are all-day rides featuring some of the best mixed-terrain riding the tri-state area has to offer. Forgotten woods roads, fast gravel, rugged singletrack, and even a bit of hike-a-bike. These rides will be long, difficult, and absolutely beautiful. While there is no perfect bike for a Sunday Epic, anything with around a 2 inch tire will work. More details on terrain will be included in each event post. Sunday Epic's will be held the third Sunday of every month from April-September. Start location may vary, but will usually end will some sort of food and drink situation. Wheels down at 8am always.

 This one is gonna be extra tough. Bring a mountain bike of some sort, curly bars may not get you far. My goal here was to put together a ride with the toughest possible terrain and most amount of climbing in the least mileage. Enter the Grass Mtn Sufferset. If you've never visited this area you are in for a treat. Starts and ends at the Shaftsbury Historical Society on 7A, park by the red barn.

 

A few notes on the nitty-gritty of these rides. 

  • Sunday Epic's are fully self supported. Bring everything you need to successfully finish the route. We expect you to carry basics like spare tube, pump, multi-tool, patch kit, food and water, etc. Although we occasionally stop at a convenience store, there are many times where the ride is too remote for that to be an option.
  • We generally try to ride together, but you are welcome to do your own thing as long as you have the route. Group pace usually hovers somewhere around the 10mph average mark, but may be slower depending on terrain/climbing.
  • Expect this to take a good chunk of the day. Occasional stops for snacks etc. We move pretty continuously, but also aren't in a rush. 

RideWithGPS link here.

Note that we don't charge anything for these rides, but we do welcome donations! We are a community-based 501c3 nonprofit focused on removing barriers to cycling for all within the tri-state area. We provide education, free access to bikes and cycling accessories, and provide a place for people of all ages and abilities to connect through cycling. Road racing is back in a big way. Join us east of Belvidere, IL for the Boone County Road Race.  This will be a joint USAC Road Race State Championship for both Illinois and Wisconsin. This title hasn't been awarded in Illinois for almost ten years—don't miss your chance to claim it.

Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available. 

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

COVID 19: Please do not join our events if you have recently tested positive, been around someone who's tested positive, or you are not feeling well.
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 9:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

About DRRT:

Dirt Rock n Root Training's owner Kathi Krause has been around the bike block – from velodrome and road racing to cyclocross, XC and finally her true love: downhill. She spent a decade on the Pro downhill circuit, stacking up three Masters World DH Championships, five national titles and a win at the legendary Kamikaze Downhill.

After 25 years of racing, Kathi shifted gears to coaching and founded Dirt Rock n Root Training in 2011 . Since then, she's been helping riders find their flow on everything from lift-accessed bike parks to rocky, rooty singletrack. Women's Cyclocross Skills Clinic — Northeast Ohio Cyclocross

Sunday, August 30th | 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM

Whether you're brand new to 'cross or looking to sharpen your handling before race day, this clinic is your chance to build confidence on the bike in a fun, low-pressure setting. All levels are welcome — this is the most accessible discipline in cycling, and there's no better way to try it out or level up your skills.

We're building a mini-course covering every core cyclocross skill: mounts and dismounts, barriers, cornering, carries, cambers, and starts. You'll work through each skill station with course breakdown, bike handling tips, and hands-on coach feedback along the way.

This clinic will be held rain or shine — both are part of racing 'cross, so come dressed for the weather and ready to ride. We do have a pavilion to take breaks and keep gear dry!

Tove Shere

It's a race against the clock! The Calaveras Time Trial by Team Fremont is a great race for everyone of all different skill levels on the beautiful Calaveras Road in Sunol, CA. Whether you are a seasoned road racer, triathlete, a junior racer or a beginner, we have a category for you.

REGISTRATION: Online Registration ONLY. Closes midnight, Thursday August 27. 2026. Entry are fees $50 except Juniors Cat $20, fees include $3 NCNCA and $5.99 USAC insurance surcharges. The Calaveras TT is part of the NCNCA BAR/BAT, NCNCA Juniors Series & the 2025 NCNCA Junior District TT Championship.

DIRECTIONS: From I-680, take the Highway 84 exit and go north on Paloma Road (84) to Sunol. Bear left on 84 onto Niles Canyon road and then turn right on to Main Street to Sunol Glen School. Follow signs to parking. From Niles Canyon (Fremont), exit at Sunol turn right on Main Street. Follow signs to parking.

COURSE: 10 miles on excellent to fair pavement, this is an out and back course. One major climb of 350 feet going to the turn. Start and finish are located approx. 300 yards South of I-680 on Calaveras Road. Turn at the 5.0 miles mark, 1 mile up the hill and past Geary road and retrace. Juniors 9-10 will have a 5 mile course.

WARM UP: Trainer or rollers. No warming up on course.

RULES: USAC Permit 202X-XXXX. A 2026 USAC license required, or purchase a 1-day license during pre-registration or on Bike Reg. No time trial bikes are allowed for all Junior Categories, see USAC Rule 1I5 pg. 31. All USA Cycling rules and code of conduct will be enforced. Juniors 15-18 up may use Time Trial Bikes in non-junior categories. MERCKX: no aero bars or clip-ons, no TT helmet (or face shield), and no wheels deeper than 60mm (paying homage to how Merckx set the hour record in 1972). All other categories may use Time Trial Bikes (except U14).

Start times will be posted at OnTheDay.net 

We'll email you a link to the start lists on August 28th. First rider will depart the start at 8:01 and following riders will depart in the above category order at 60 second intervals. Field limited to 360 total start slots due to parking constraints.

SECOND RIDES: There will be a break after the Junior categories to enable as many 2nd rides as possible. Race Merckx or Masters before the break and your category after the break.

Welcome to the first annual Interlude 360 mile ultra bike race! 

22+ miles of single track - 92 miles of pavement - 246+ miles of gravel and B roads

Start Location - Red Wheel Bike shop - 400 West Main Street Jefferson City, Missouri 65101

Starting time - 0900 - Friday - September 4th 2026  (Registration Sign in will begin at 08:00 am)

Rules

Every year the rules can change. The fastest participant is usually the one that knows the rules.

This is not a closed course you are responsible for your person and all belongings you take or acquire along the way. You will have to carry your bike at some time. You could definitely get your feet wet. everyone and any one that may be affiliated with Red wheel Bike shop and Interlude bike race is not held liable for any of your actions before, during, or after this event.

Drafting is allowed

No littering

Every Participant must utilize a front and rear light at night.

If you go off course you must reenter at the same place. 

You can secure a sleeping arrangement before the begins.

Everyone is allowed to have support during the event. This means food, water and even utilizing a vehicle to sleep in. Hopefully this will allow beginner and new ultra cyclists to  test their abilities before jumping into a even bigger event.

Don't be a dick!

Allowed - 

  • Aero bars
  • Super Tuck
  • Super Aero helmets
  • Any width of handlebars
  • Drop bar mountain bikes
  • Any sock height

Race route - The route will start at Jefferson City and move north to Macon, Missouri and circle back.

This is the unofficial route.

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/55489174

*August 1st the race route will be posted on the internet and e-mailed to all participants. 

Popular Questions: 

Will there be aid stations? No you will need to bring or purchase every thing you need to survive.

What type of bike will I need? That is up to you! As race director, I believe a gravel bike with a minimum of 45mm tires will be needed. I would not recommend a road bike. Any mountain bike would work.

Is there a cut off time to finish?  No  - If you take longer than 72 hours you will be considered a finisher but no one will be at the finish line to meet you. 

Will there be SAG if I can't finish? Yes, If you need help getting back to the finish line for any uncertain reason a SAG driver will be of assistance. Please understand you could be waiting a while if you are at the other end of the course. Once you decide you can not finish the course you are considered DNF. You are able to have help from any friends, team or family. 

Where can I sleep on the course? Sleeping is always an option. Motels, AIRBB, VRBO, AND campsites are preferred. If you decide to sleep any where else know the law. Don't Trespass. Stay out of ditches. Be aware of your surroundings. You are welcome to sleep in a sag drivers vehicle. 

Can I ride without a Spot Tracker? No, The Spot Tracker is not only for friends and family to follow you but also for safety.

RACE RULES!!!! WE ARE NOW A PART OF THE CHAINBUSTER'S ENDURANCE SERIES!!! FOR SPECIFIC RULES CHECK OUT CHAINBUSTER'S RULES

All participants will be required to wear a bicycle helmet at all times while riding. Penalty is DQ.

Outside (non racer) assistance is only permitted in the pit area. Non racers may not assist out on the course. Racers may assist other racers and are encouraged to do so.

All food and drink for the race must be either carried with the racer or staged in the pit area. There will be 1 water stop on the course as well.

Due to the number of racers on the trail, earbuds are prohibited.

Race numbers must be visible at all times and must be mounted to the handlebars on the front of the bike.

Littering is not permitted. First offense is 15 minute penalty, 2nd offense is DQ.

Cutting the course is not permitted. Penalty is DQ and public ridicule.

In the event of an unfixable mechanical, the racer must complete the lap along the entire course with his/her bike to receive credit for the lap. You MAY back track or shortcut back to the pit to fix your bike, but you will not receive credit for that lap. Do not enter the timing/exchange area if you are coming back from an incomplete lap. Please be honest.

Please exercise caution and good sportsmanship when passing other racers on the trail. Announce your intention to pass rather than just forcing your way by with no warning. Most riders will gladly let you pass.

Solos need to complete one lap to be considered official finishers. Teams need each person to complete at least one lap to be considered official finishers.

Once you reach your pit, you may change any equipment you want, including bikes, and you may stay there as long as you'd like.

WINNERS WILL BE DETERMINED BY NUMBER OF LAPS COMPLETED IN THE GIVEN TIME. IF MULTIPLE RIDERS HAVE THE SAME NUMBER OF LAPS THEN LAP TIMES WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE WINNER!

4) Participant support - NO - you can NOT follow your "rider" around the course to support. You CAN sign up to help at an aid station and HELP ALL THE RIDERS. Our agreement with the USFS to minimally impact the Forest is paramount. And this is the only way we can do our part to limit our footprint and not disrupt the sensitive balance of life and user access during this event weekend. Rider disqualification will result if outside support is noted or reported.

    The Shenandoah Mountain 100 is one of the most popular courses in the NUE Series. Your entry fee includes aid stations 20 miles apart along the course. Cash purse listed below. Class categories: Men and Women Open, Singlespeed, U 19 (Juniors), Masters (50+), Tandem, and Clydesdale. All competitors will receive a technical t-shirt and participant pint glass.

    CAMPING - We recommended reserving a site at the host venue - Stokesville Campground - for the full 3-day weekend or at Natural Chimney Campground. If sites are not available on those portals, then camping is full. Participants can set up shop for their respective event in the Observatory field for the event.

    We have a drop system organized where you can arrange to have supplies (lights, gear, food, etc.) left at the aid stations. You are allowed TWO (100K) or FOUR (100 MILER)- 1 gallon ziploc bags to be used as drop bags that we will provide. That includes your lights!!!! If the ziploc cannot seal closed we will not send it onto the aid stations. No camelbak drops allowed unless it fits in one closed gallon ziploc bag.  They must be labeled with race number and are to be dropped off no later than 1 hour before the event start. They cannot be picked up again until the evening at the end of the race. If you are unable to pick up your supplies, we can mail them back to you for $30. We are not responsible for any lost, stolen or missing drop bags.

AID STATIONS:

The aid stations' high spirits will keep you rolling and having fun all day. When stopping at a station please do not drop your bike in the road, either keep it between your legs or walk it to the side of the road and so it isn't in the way of other Forest users.

    We are in a tough spot with spectators - we can't have them at the Campground or out on the course - there just isn't physically room to park extra cars. But we need some volunteers. So if you have family that "MUST ATTEND" we can put them to use as a volunteer. We have some great volunteer spots that could use their help. THIS YEAR MORE THEN EVER non racers MUST volunteer. Volunteers are a great aspect to this event as well as all of our other events, so please help out. 

Station #1: 11 miles in - approx. 1-2 hours - Bottom of Tillman West on Tillman Rd.
NO DROP BAGS ALLOWED - Water - You will have to stop while we fill your bottle. You will have to take off the lid and hold it yourself. We will have a pump and some mechanical supplies. You will have the climb up Lynn and roll the downhill on Wolf before station #2

Station #2: NEW LOCATION 24.5 miles - approx. 2 to 3 1/2 hours - Wolf Ridge Parking Lot
Station will be stocked with food and beverages to be announced at a later time.

Station #3: 45 miles in - approx. 3 1/2 to 5 hours - Bottom of Dowell's Draft (last 100K station)
Anything but specific food is discouraged. Station will be stocked with food and beverages to be announced at a later time.

Station #4: 57 miles in - approx. 4 1/2 to 6 1/2 hours – Cold Coke Braley Pond
Anything but specific food is discouraged. Station will be stocked with food and beverages to be announced at a later time. <This station is not in the 100K route>

Station #5: 75 miles in - approx. 5 1/2 to 10 hours -- Cold Coke Shen Mtn Picnic Area
No one is permitted to continue past this section without lights and or approval from the boss past 4:20 PM. Warm clothes are suggested if you think you will be out after dark. 6:00 PM is the cut off even if you have lights. <This station is not in the 100K route>

Station #6: 88 miles in - approx. 7 to 14 hours - Bottom of Chestnut/Skidmore
Additional lights may be needed at this point. If you have been riding from #5 in the dark it will take you at least 2 hours to finish the race in the dark. The leaders can do the last section in about 1 hour during daylight. <This station is not in the 100K route>

Down for Gravel

Date: Saturday, September 5, 2026

Location: 101 Applegate Lane, West Newfield, Maine


 

Event Overview:

Down for Gravel is a gravel cycling event that brings riders together for a challenging and rewarding day on the backroads of western Maine. The start and finish are situated on the picturesque Mirror Lake, providing a scenic backdrop for the day’s ride. Routes wind through forest roads, rolling terrain, and offer stunning views—including glimpses of Mount Washington on clear days. Whether you’re looking to push your limits or enjoy a solid day of riding with great company, this event is all about community and the shared experience of gravel cycling.


 

Riders can choose from multiple route options to match their goals for the day. Each course is designed to provide a mix of smooth gravel, rugged sections, and plenty of climbing. The ride is untimed—this is about the experience, not the results.


 

Sunday Cyclocross & Camping:

The weekend kicks off on Saturday with a gravel ride, trail running race and cyclocross clinics.  Offering fast-paced action and a great opportunity to warm up or spectate before Sunday CX race. Riders are encouraged to camp on-site Friday and Saturday night to soak in the atmosphere, connect with fellow cyclists, and make the most of the weekend. The event setup includes a large open field with plenty of space for camping and parking, creating a festival-like setting leading up to race day.


 

Post-Ride Gathering:

After Down For Gravel on Saturday, stick around to share stories, enjoy wood-fired pizza, and relax with a cold beer from Frost Beer Works. A post-ride swim in Mirror Lake is highly recommended—there’s no better way to cool down after a long day on the bike.


 

Location & Accessibility:

West Newfield is conveniently located about an hour’s drive from Portland, Maine, and less than two hours from Boston, making it an easy weekend getaway for gravel riders from across the region.


 

Registration:

Sign up to secure your spot. Space is limited, and early registration is encouraged.


 

Pinebury is proud to support Down for Gravel, helping to create an event that brings people together over a shared love of gravel riding, adventure, and fun.

The 2nd annual Tour D' Athens will start and end at First United Methodist Church in Athens.  We have four routes to choose from this year:   Metric Century, 55-mile, 30-mile, and a 22-mile route. Rest stops will be between 10-15 miles, and we will have bike mechanics along the routes to help with minor repairs.

 

**Register by August 15,2026 to be guaranteed a t-shirt.  The event t-shirt is a large part of our cost. In order to keep cost to a minimum, we will only order a small surplus of extra shirts. We will only be able to exchange t-shirt sizes if there is one available in the surplus pile. **

Schedule of events:

  • Onsite packet pick up opens at 6am
  • Metric Century and 55 mile route riders take off at 7:30 am
  • 30 and 22 mile route riders take off 5 min after

 

 

         ROUTES WILL BE POSTED ON OUR WEBSITE WWW.ATHENSBIKERIDE.COM

 

** Rest stops and support will stop at 4 pm. We will make one last sweep of each route and offer the sag wagon, or you can press on and finish on your own. **

Please check out our website at www.athensbikeride.com for updates and additional information about the ride.

 

Inclement Weather Policy

We strive to produce a full and safe bicycle rally, but sometimes the weather conditions can impact those plans. We encourage all participants to arrive as scheduled on the morning of the ride as weather condition-related decisions will be made shortly before the ride start time of 8 AM. In many instances, weather conditions in one part of the State may not be impacting the event location, or weather conditions may improve in the hours preceding the event, both of which impact the ride start. In the event of light to moderate rain, and in the absence of any lightning, our goal is to proceed with the full event if road conditions are safe and will allow the bike ride to take place. If there is lightning in the area, the event will be placed into a weather hold and can be held for up to one hour. If the lightning has departed the area after one hour, the ride can proceed as planned. If there is still evidence of the potential for lightning in the area, the ride may either be shortened or canceled. The event has a one-hour weather hold time frame because the schedule impacts the safety of the event by such factors as increasing traffic on the routes as the day passes, and law enforcement and medical support schedules.

Due to the nature of bike rides taking place generally in the outdoors, weather conditions can play a large role in the production of the event. Because a significant amount of the funds collected during registration have already been expended by the day of the event, and because each event is uniquely scheduled for its date and location, registration refunds are not possible, and rescheduling the event is not feasible, therefore we have a no refund policy. We encourage all those who are pre-registered to pick up their packets with the t-shirt. T-shirts will not be mailed. Proceeds from registration fees and donations will continue to benefit the HALO fund. Thank you for your understanding of these policies. We appreciate your participation.

The Knobby Rock Gravel Grinder is a gravel bicycle event that highlights an incredible series of dirt loops in the heart of the Green Mountains and traverses through the scenic Moosalamoo National Recreation Area. The ride starts as a mass start from the iconic Blueberry Hill Inn and Outdoor Center located in the heart of the Moosalamoo forest. The course is primarily hard packed gravel and dirt roads and a few short sections of multi-use trail.

Riders will enjoy post race grill out, and camping is included on site, both the night before and after the event.
